subject: health
unitTitle: Food, Water, and Moving My Body
title: Guided practice: hunger and fullness signals
essentialQuestion: How do food, water, and movement give my body energy for the things I want to do?
materials: paper or a digital planner for day plans
keyPoints: The body sends signals: a rumbling or empty stomach, low energy, or trouble concentrating.
Fullness arrives slowly, so eating at a steady pace helps you notice it.
Being hungry between meals is normal and is what snacks are for.
Different days need different amounts, and that is expected, not a problem to fix.
privacySafeScenario: Kai finishes lunch quickly and still feels hungry, then feels uncomfortably full ten minutes later. What might explain that?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about hunger and fullness signals to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Using the practice situation, say what the safest or healthiest next step is and why.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about hunger and fullness signals.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Plans may use pictures, cut-outs, dictation, or spoken description. Learners with food allergies, medical diets, religious or cultural food practices, or limited food access plan with the foods actually available to them, and the adult may substitute any example.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about hunger and fullness signals under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, look at what the household already keeps for quick snacks and talk about which ones travel well. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
